    agent-device find "Home"

  If apps lookup misses the project but shows Expo Go/dev-client and a project URL is available, open the URL/host shell; if no URL is available, ask instead of inventing an app id.
  Expo Dev Client/development builds: open the installed dev-client app id/name; if a dev-client URL is provided, open that URL next. For Metro setup use metro prepare --kind expo.

  help debugging       logs, network, alerts, traces, flaky runtime failures
  help react-devtools  React Native performance, profiling, props/state/hooks, slow renders, rerenders
  help react-native   React Native app automation hazards, overlays, Metro, and routing
  help remote          remote/cloud config, tenant, lease, local service tunnels
  help macos           desktop, frontmost-app, menu bar surfaces
  help dogfood         exploratory QA report workflow

  agent-device help                  command list and global flags
  agent-device help <command>        command-specific flags
  agent-device help workflow         normal app automation loop

The XCTest runner is failing with "kAXErrorIllegalArgument getting snapshot for element ... pid=88279". The app (pid 88279) is publishing an unhealthy accessibility tree, and XCTest's tap path requires a snapshot of the app element to resolve the tap target. The private-ax backend can read the tree (that's how snapshot worked), but XCTest's native tap fails.

Interesting point: the earlier taps succeeded (150,181), (197,232), @e27 — those were against the old app instance (pid 85887). After the relaunch, the new app instance (pid 88279) also has an unhealthy AX tree, and now the XCTest tap consistently fails.

Wait, but the earlier successful taps were also against pid 85887, which had the same kAXErrorIllegalArgument issue (the snapshot warning mentioned pid=85887). And yet the taps at (150,181), (197,232) succeeded... hmm, actually those taps "succeeded" (ok=1) but didn't change the UI. Maybe they weren't actually landing on the app? No wait — they were reported as Tapped and ok=1 in the runner log.

Hmm, actually the earlier successful taps were... let me double-check. In the runner log from earlier, the tap command completed with ok=1. But the UI didn't change (the Feeds screen stayed as is). So those taps were landing somewhere but not on an interactive element — or the coordinates were wrong.

Now, after the relaunch, the tap at (79, 591) fails with kAXErrorIllegalArgument. The difference: the new runner instance is failing to find the app element.

The skill guidance says: "If snapshot returns a sparse/AX-unavailable state, refs are unreliable. Use plain screenshots instead of screenshot --overlay-refs, navigate with coordinates if needed, then retry snapshot -i after reaching a different screen. The AX failure may be screen-specific."

Also: "Rare iOS accessibility gaps: ... run agent-device snapshot -i --json to read the rects, compute the target center, press x y, then diff snapshot -i. Coordinates are fallback only."

The XCTest tap path is failing because the app's AX tree is unhealthy. But agent-device has a "private-ax accessibility backend" for snapshots. Maybe there's also a fallback tap path via the helper (e.g., simctl or a touch helper). The workflow help mentioned "the bundled touch helper" for Android. For iOS, the tap goes through XCTest.

Let me check `agent-device help debugging` for guidance on this failure mode.
